newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia indignant at Trans-World attack - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Russia indignant at Trans-World attack - Interfax.

text.p: Russia's government reacted with indignation to an open letter from commodity firm Trans-World Group on foreign involvement in Russia's aluminium industry, Interfax news agency quoted a cabinet source as saying on Friday.
"This document can provoke nothing but indignation," said the source, familiar with the text of the Trans-World letter.
London-based Trans-World is a major commodity firm which has a large stake in some of Russia's biggest aluminium plants.

Chairman David Reuben published an open letter to U.S. Vice President Albert Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in several newspapers this week attacking what he said were moves by Russia to "reprivatise" the industry.
Reuben described the move as "a craven, politicial power play, Russian style."
"This power play is aimed at confiscating certain foreign investments without due process," the letter said.

The cabinet source denied categorically Reuben's suggestion that the future placement of large foreign firms in the Russian metals industry was tied to the future of Trans-World in Russia, Interfax said.

The strong attack from Trans-World, a privately held company, appears to have been triggered by calls last month from Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov to curb foreign ownership in the aluminium industry.
Kulikov also said Russia should consider slapping duties on imports of raw materials used in primary aluminium production.
Russia is the world's biggest aluminium exporter, and delivered 2.44 million tonnes to world markets in 1996.

Trans-World Group investments in Russia are on hold until the Russian government announces an official position on the minister's call to curb foreign ownership of the aluminium industry, a director of the firm said in London on Friday.
